title: Presheaf point pullback on affine objects
statement: Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $\mathbf{Prof}$ have compact Hausdorff totally disconnected spaces as objects and continuous maps as arrows, with finite jointly surjective coverings. For $S\in\mathbf{Prof}$, let $X[S]$ be the inverse limit over the finite continuous quotients $S\to S_i$ of the finite disjoint unions $\coprod_{S_i}X$, and let $a_X(S)=X[S]$. For a sheaf $F$ of sets, abelian groups, or commutative rings on $\mathbf{Prof}$, let $P_F$ be the presheaf left Kan extension of its underlying presheaf along $a_X^{op}$, so $P_F(V)=\operatorname{colim}_{(V\to X[S])}F(S)$, with transitions induced by precomposition on $F$. For every affine object $V$, the quotient space $\pi_0(|V|)$ of connected components, with quotient topology, is profinite, and there is a canonical isomorphism $P_F(V)\cong F(\pi_0(|V|))$, natural in $F$ and in affine $V$. In particular, for every finite family of affine objects $V_i$, the restriction map $P_F(\coprod_iV_i)\to\prod_iP_F(V_i)$ is an isomorphism, including the empty family. The isomorphisms preserve the indicated algebraic operations.
